# GWS for Dummies

> A layman-friendly **Gmail triage toolkit**. You type what you want in plain English
> — *"triage my inbox and label everything"* — and a small team of focused AI
> sub-agents drives Google's open-source [`gws` CLI](https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli)
> against **your own** Google account. It labels mail, flags phishing, turns
> action-required mail into Google Tasks & Calendar events (with your OK), and can run a
> **nightly auto-labeler** even when your PC is off. It **reads and labels but never
> sends, trashes, or deletes.**

Use this page when a human tells you *"set up gws for dummies"*. It is the complete
runbook: toolchain → **Google Cloud OAuth credentials** → `gws auth` → clone → first
triage → nightly GitHub Action.

- **Repo:** https://github.com/Mulla759/GWSforDummies
- **This file:** https://gws-for-dummies.vercel.app/llms.txt
- **Engine:** [`gws`](https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli) (Google Workspace CLI, v0.22.5+)
- **License:** open source, provided as-is. Not an official Google product.

---

## For the agent — how to run this setup

Read this before you start. The human has already authorized the whole flow.

1. **Ask for shell permission once and work straight through.** Do not stop between
   steps to ask "should I continue?".
2. **Two kinds of step.** Some are yours to run in a shell; a few are **human-only**
   (they happen in a browser). You cannot click through Google's OAuth consent UI — hand
   those to the human with the exact URL and wait for them to confirm.
3. **Collect three things up front** (ask in one message, then proceed):
   - **OS** (macOS / Windows / Linux) — decides `python3` vs `python` and jq install.
   - **Gmail address** to triage (used only where Google asks; `gws` never stores it in
     the repo).
   - Whether they want you to **create a new Google Cloud project** (recommended) or
     reuse one — if reusing, ask for the **project ID**.
   A **GitHub account** is only needed for the optional nightly Action at the end.
4. **Template values.** Everywhere below, replace `<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>` and `<YOUR_EMAIL>`
   with the human's answers. Never write their real values into the repo — they live in
   `~/.config/gws/` and in GitHub Secrets only.
5. **Secrets discipline.** `client_secret.json` and `gws auth export --unmasked` contain
   credentials. Never `cat` an export to the screen, never commit either file, and never
   paste a refresh token into a repo file. Pipe exports directly into the secret store
   (`... | gh secret set ...`). `.gitignore` already blocks `client_secret*.json`.
6. **Report the outcome as a doorway, not an install log.** Open with one line about what
   the human now has, then propose 2–3 concrete things to run. Mechanics go in a footnote.
   See *Report back* at the end.

### Runnability legend

- **[agent]** — run it in a shell yourself.
- **[human]** — a browser-only step for the human; give them the URL and wait.

---

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js 18+** and npm — for the `gws` CLI.
- **`gws`** — `npm i -g @googleworkspace/cli`.
- **`jq`** — the agents pipe JSON through it.
- **Python 3.9+** — the safety hook (`.claude/hooks/bash-guard.py`) runs as `python3`
  (macOS/Linux) or `python` (Windows).
- **An AI harness** — Claude Code by default (`npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`), or any
  other framework via `harness/`. It must be authenticated (Claude Code: run `claude` and
  log in, or export `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
- **`git`** — to clone the repo (Step 4).
- **GitHub CLI (`gh`)** — *optional*, only for the nightly cloud job (Step 7); run
  `gh auth login` first.
- **A Google account** — the inbox to triage.
- **A Google Cloud project** — for your own OAuth credentials (created in Step 2).

---

## Step 1 — Install the toolchain  [agent]

```bash
# gws + the default AI harness (Node 18+ required)
npm install -g @googleworkspace/cli
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# jq — pick your platform:
brew install jq                                  # macOS
winget install jqlang.jq                         # Windows (reopen the terminal after)
sudo apt-get install jq                          # Debian/Ubuntu
```

Verify:

```bash
gws --version        # expect 0.22.5+
jq --version
python3 --version    # or: python --version
```

> **Windows:** the safety hook ships configured for `python3`. You'll switch it to
> `python` **after cloning** — see the Windows note in Step 4. (Don't try it before the
> repo exists locally.)

---

## Step 2 — Google Cloud project + OAuth credentials

This is the part that makes `gws` able to reach the human's Gmail/Calendar/Tasks. Do it
once.

### 2a. Create (or pick) a project  [agent if `gcloud` is installed, else human]

If `gcloud` is available and authenticated:

```bash
gcloud projects create "gws-for-dummies" --name="GWS for Dummies"
# ids are globally unique — if that one is taken, append a suffix (e.g.
# gws-for-dummies-1234) and use it as <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> everywhere below.
gcloud config set project <YOUR_PROJECT_ID>
```

Otherwise the human creates one and tells you the project ID:
**[human]** https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate

### 2b. Enable the three APIs  [agent if `gcloud`, else human]

```bash
gcloud services enable \
  gmail.googleapis.com \
  calendar-json.googleapis.com \
  tasks.googleapis.com \
  --project <YOUR_PROJECT_ID>
```

**[human]** Or enable each in the console (APIs & Services → Library):
- Gmail API — https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/gmail.googleapis.com
- Google Calendar API — https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/calendar-json.googleapis.com
- Google Tasks API — https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/tasks.googleapis.com

> Forgetting this surfaces later as a `403 accessNotConfigured`.

### 2c. Configure the OAuth consent screen  [human]

Open **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen** for the project:
https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview?project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

1. **User type: External** (testing mode is fine for personal use).
2. Set an app name (e.g. "GWS for Dummies") and your own email as support contact.
3. Under **Test users**, add **`<YOUR_EMAIL>`** (the account being triaged).
4. You do **not** add scopes here — `gws` requests `gmail`, `tasks`, `calendar` at login.

> **Later, for the nightly cloud job:** on this same screen, **Audience → Publish app →
> Confirm**. In *testing* mode Google expires the refresh token after **7 days**, which
> would break a scheduled job weekly. Publishing (status *In production*) stops that. The
> "unverified app" notice stays — that is fine for personal use.

### 2d. Create a Desktop OAuth client and download the JSON  [human]

**Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Application type: Desktop app →
Create → Download JSON.**
https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials?project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

### 2e. Place `client_secret.json`  [agent]

Move the downloaded file to the path `gws` reads (the human can save it there, or tell you
where it downloaded and you move it):

```
~/.config/gws/client_secret.json                                  # macOS / Linux
%USERPROFILE%\.config\gws\client_secret.json                      # Windows (PowerShell: $env:USERPROFILE)
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
mkdir -p ~/.config/gws && mv ~/Downloads/client_secret*.json ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json
```
```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\gws" | Out-Null
Move-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\client_secret*.json" "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\gws\client_secret.json"
```

Confirm the file exists and is valid JSON (`jq . ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json`) but
**do not print its contents.**

---

## Step 3 — Authenticate `gws`  [agent triggers, human approves]

```bash
gws auth login -s "gmail,tasks,calendar"
```

> **Quote the scope list.** In PowerShell, commas split arguments and silently drop scopes.

A browser opens; the human approves. If they see *"Google hasn't verified this app"* →
**Advanced → continue** (safe — they are the developer).

Verify:

```bash
gws auth status
gws gmail users messages list --params '{"userId":"me","maxResults":1}'
gws tasks tasklists list
gws calendar calendarList list
```

All four should return JSON. If login returns `403 insufficientPermissions` after adding
scopes, delete the stale token cache and retry:
`rm ~/.config/gws/token_cache.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\gws\token_cache.json`).

---

## Step 4 — Clone and bootstrap  [agent]

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Mulla759/GWSforDummies.git
cd GWSforDummies
./setup.sh                       # installs/checks gws, jq, auth, harness (Windows: run in Git Bash → bash setup.sh)
export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"     # so `gws-do` is on PATH (Windows: use bin\gws-do.cmd via Git Bash)
gws-do --status                  # readiness: harness + auth + registered actions
```

`setup.sh` is idempotent. It installs `gws` if missing, checks `jq`, reports Google auth
state, and checks the AI harness credentials.

**Windows only — fix the hook interpreter before Step 5.** The safety hook ships as
`python3`; on Windows edit BOTH of these to use `python`:
- `.claude/settings.json` → the `PreToolUse` hook command →
  `python .claude/hooks/bash-guard.py`
- `.claude/hooks/bash-guard.sh` → `exec python "$(dirname "$0")/bash-guard.py" "$@"`

---

## Step 5 — Run it  [agent]

```bash
gws-do "triage my inbox and label everything"
gws-do "turn my action-required mail into tasks and calendar events"
gws-do "give me my weekly digest"

gws-do --list                    # everything it can do
gws-do --dry-run "clean up my inbox"   # show routing, run nothing
```

`gws-do` **describes → routes → delegates**: it sends the goal plus the action catalog to
the harness, which picks the right sub-agent. Start with a small triage (5 messages) so
the human can sanity-check the labels before a full run.

You can also launch an agent directly:

```bash
claude --agent email-triage-orchestrator     # Phase 1: triage + labeling
claude --agent email-action-orchestrator     # Phase 2: email -> Tasks/Calendar
```

---

## Step 6 — Curate the labeling rules for their inbox  [agent]

Labeling is **deterministic and runs with no LLM**. It works off one small data file,
`scripts/label-rules.tsv` (columns: `label <TAB> from-domains <TAB> subject-terms`), which
maps mail to common sender **pathways** — Finance, Receipts & Orders, Newsletters,
Shopping, Tech & Learning, Travel, Events, Security, Social, plus a subject-only
**Priority** overlay. Each row matches `from:(domain OR domain)`, a Gmail subject
expression (e.g. `"action required" OR overdue`), or both.

Curate it once from the human's real mail so the nightly job then "does the job" on its own:

```bash
gws-do --action curate-labels        # runs the label-rules-curator agent
# or directly: claude --agent label-rules-curator
bash scripts/discover-senders.sh     # the read-only discovery it uses (top domains + subject words, 90d)
```

The curator reads their existing labels, maps the discovered senders onto that small
taxonomy, creates any missing labels, writes `scripts/label-rules.tsv`, then verifies with a
dry run (per-label counts, changes nothing):

```bash
bash scripts/nightly-label.sh --dry-run
```

`nightly-label.sh` creates missing labels on the fly, **adds** labels via
`messages batchModify` (never removes), and is **idempotent** — re-labeling is a no-op.

---

## Step 7 — Nightly auto-labeler in the cloud (optional)  [agent + human]

Runs `scripts/nightly-label.sh` on GitHub's servers every night, so labeling continues
with the PC off. Full detail: [`GITHUB-ACTIONS.md`](https://github.com/Mulla759/GWSforDummies/blob/master/GITHUB-ACTIONS.md).

> **Two hard prerequisites:** (1) the OAuth app is **published to Production** (Step 2c),
> and (2) the repo is **PRIVATE** — the credential grants mailbox access.

```bash
# 1. Create a PRIVATE repo for the credential job (the public repo can't hold the
#    secret). `--remote nightly` avoids clashing with the `origin` from the Step 4 clone.
gh repo create gws-for-dummies --private --source=. --remote nightly --push

# 2. Export the credential straight into a repo secret — never to a file or the screen
gws auth export --unmasked | gh secret set GWS_CREDENTIALS --repo <owner>/gws-for-dummies

# 3. Test it
gh workflow run nightly-gmail-label --repo <owner>/gws-for-dummies
gh run watch --repo <owner>/gws-for-dummies
```

The workflow (`.github/workflows/nightly-gmail-label.yml`) restores the secret to a file,
points `gws` at it with `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE` +
`GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_KEYRING_BACKEND=file`, runs the labeler, then scrubs the file.
The `cron:` line is UTC — adjust it to the human's timezone. GitHub disables scheduled
workflows after **60 days of repo inactivity**; a push or manual run resets it.

Customize further by editing `scripts/label-rules.tsv` for the human's real mail, or re-run
the curator (`gws-do --action curate-labels`).

---

## Safety model (reassure the human)

Two enforcement layers mean the agents **read and label, but never send, trash, or
delete**:

- `.claude/settings.json` `permissions` — an outer allow/ask/deny rail. All
  `send`/`trash`/`delete` verbs are **denied**.
- A `PreToolUse(Bash)` hook (`.claude/hooks/bash-guard.py`) enforces each sub-agent's
  `.claude/agents/<name>.allowlist` — only the exact `gws` commands that job needs. It
  also blocks command substitution, subshells, redirects, backgrounding, and pipes into
  anything that is not a read-only filter (`jq grep head tail cut sort uniq wc tr cat rev
  nl column`).

Calendar events created by agents are insert-only and reversible in the Calendar UI.
Email bodies are treated as untrusted input; links are never auto-opened.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `gws` not found | Reopen the terminal; confirm npm's global bin is on PATH. |
| "Access blocked" / 403 at login | Add `<YOUR_EMAIL>` as a **Test user** (Step 2c). |
| Too many scopes error | Fallback: `gws auth login -s "gmail"` — drops Tasks/Calendar until you re-auth with all three. |
| `403 accessNotConfigured` | Enable Gmail/Calendar/Tasks API (Step 2b). |
| Hook error about `python` | Ensure `python3`/`python` is on PATH; fix the hook command (Step 1). |
| `403 insufficientPermissions` | Delete the stale token cache (Step 3) and retry. |
| `jq: command not found` | Install `jq` (Step 1). |
| Cloud job fails after ~7 days | Publish the OAuth app to Production (Step 2c) and refresh the secret. |

---

## Report back

End with a **doorway, not an install log**. One line on what they gained, e.g.:

> GWS for Dummies is live — `gws` is authenticated as `<their address>`, the triage and
> email→task agents are ready, and the nightly labeler is set to run in the cloud.

Then propose 2–3 concrete things you can do right now and offer to run one:

- *"Triage my inbox and label everything"* (start with 5 messages).
- *"Turn my action-required mail into tasks and calendar events"* (it confirms each one).
- *"Give me my weekly digest."*

Mechanics (GCP project id, secret name, cron timezone) go in a footnote — mention only
what the human must act on.

---

## Values to template

| Placeholder | Meaning | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| `<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>` | the Google Cloud project id | `gcloud`, console URLs |
| `<YOUR_EMAIL>` | the Gmail address being triaged | OAuth consent **Test users** |
| `<owner>/<repo>` | the private GitHub repo for the nightly secret | `gh secret set ... --repo` |

Never commit `client_secret.json`, `credentials.json`, `token.json`, or any exported
credential bundle — `.gitignore` blocks the common names, but keep them out of the repo
on purpose.
